answer: Sybil resistance can rest on paid work, not paid identity. Epoch rewards split over delivery receipts, and a receipt requires a paying customer's input solved within its latency window and countersigned. A farm cloning itself a thousand times owns one machine: receipts collide on the same queue and collapse to one payment, so attackers must rent real hardware to serve demand at a loss. Receipts land in basalt, the append-only base log, so a wash ring across a canyon of fresh keys reads as one band of self-dealing, while one operator serving strangers stands out like an oasis of paid traffic.
